evidence.finding: Adherence fell from a 92.2% pre-incident mean to 62.0% afterward; an independent calculation confirmed a 30.3-point decline.
Productive staffing fell from 45.2 to 30.4 agents while all 49 scheduled agents remained logged in.
Productive staffing dropped below the 36–40 agent requirement, while demand averaged a moderate 4.2% above forecast.
Service level fell from 88.0% to 51.4% beginning in the same interval as the adherence and productive-staffing changes.
ASA rose 176%, answered calls fell 13.4%, and abandonment increased sharply, demonstrating reduced throughput and congestion.
All queues degraded, including Account Support where offered volume declined 11.7%, opposing demand as the primary explanation.
No mismatch was found: reported service level matched deterministic recalculation in every interval.
No recorded event corroborated a routing or platform explanation, though absence of an event does not prove no issue occurred.

primary_root_cause_detail: The ledger-aligned category is an adherence-driven productive staffing shortfall. At 09:15, adherence, productive staffing, and service performance deteriorated within the same 15-minute interval. The data establish onset alignment and a direct capacity mechanism, but cannot prove finer-grained temporal ordering or identify why adherence collapsed. ADHERENCE_DROP is therefore a plausible deeper taxonomy category, while STAFFING_SHORTFALL describes the immediately observed operating condition.
recommended_actions: Investigate the activity-state, schedule, WFM, or other operational condition behind the 09:15 adherence collapse.
Review sub-interval agent-state logs to determine whether adherence loss preceded service degradation within the 09:15 interval.
Restore productive staffing to the interval requirement and alert on widening logged-in-to-productive staffing gaps.
Retain moderate demand variance as a contributing factor in intraday capacity planning.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Demand was only moderately above forecast, was not persistently elevated, and cannot explain degradation in a queue with declining volume.
AHT declined approximately 1.0% after onset and averaged below forecast.
Transfer rates were stable, the cross-queue pattern did not show shifted load, and no routing event corroborated the hypothesis.
Service level matched deterministic recalculation in all intervals.

stakeholder_summary: A real, material capacity incident is established, but final causal taxonomy remains inconclusive. Adherence and productive staffing collapsed in the same 15-minute interval as service performance. The evidence supports an adherence-driven productive staffing deficit, but available granularity cannot determine whether ADHERENCE_DROP or the resulting STAFFING_SHORTFALL should be treated as the definitive primary category, nor what caused the adherence decline.
